data.title: Paramount wraps up mega Warner Bros merger to create Hollywood powerhouse Skydance
data.description: Paramount Skydance completed its blockbuster $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery on Tuesday, creating a Hollywood heavyweight that hands CEO David Ellison control of one of the world's ​largest entertainment and news businesses. The Ellison family has notably held a long relationship with Republican President Donald Trump, who said that Skydance is “going to be a great company.”

data.description:

Andrew Chang explains how the fall of the incumbent Coalition Avenir Québec led to the rise of the Parti Québécois and its leader, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, and why sovereignty became a separate issue for voters.

data.title: I see what’s happening here in Paris: reasonable student demands met with awful violence | Helen Massy-Beresford
data.description: The debate around the schools protests is angry and polarised. I fear this is a foretaste of how election tensions next year will play out Helen Massy-Beresford is a British journalist who lives in Paris It would be tough to argue that the demands of France’s protesting high school students are not reasonable ones, worth taking to the streets for: investment in crumbling schools , replacing absent teachers, reducing class sizes and overstuffed timetables, and bridging the inequality gap between schools in different areas. The protests across the country on Tuesday, which demonstrators dubbed l’acte III (Act 3), or la grande mobilisation, were billed as the most dramatic day of action yet, with more school blockades and a march through central Paris in the afternoon. More than 400 schools closed preventively , including my elder daughter’s, a combined collège (for 11- to 15-year-olds) and lycée. Helen Massy-Beresford is a British journalist and editor who lives in Paris Continue reading...

data.title: The generation raised on sugar rations – and what their health reveals 70 years later
data.description: From blood pressure to ageing, research suggests the first 1,000 days of sugar exposure could leave a decades-long mark on health They were born into a Britain still recovering from the hardships of war. Though the air-raid sirens had fallen silent, many everyday foods remained rationed, including sugar. Adults were restricted to about 3 tablespoons (40g) a day to stretch between cups of tea, baking and desserts; children were limited to less than a tablespoon. Babies and very young children were expected to have little or no added sugar. Then, in 1953, the brakes came off. Separate restrictions on sweets and chocolate were lifted in February, followed by sugar in September. By the second half of 1954, average sugar consumption had almost doubled. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘All I want to do is cry’: trauma of 7 October survivors three years after the attacks
data.description: Israeli communities shattered by Hamas massacres are torn between rebuilding their lives and remembering lost friends and relatives Keith Siegel spent many of his long hours in Hamas captivity in Gaza etching everything that happened after 7 October 2023 into his memory. For 484 days, he recited to himself every place he was held, the dates he was moved and every attack or humiliation he endured or witnessed. He aimed to store intelligence that could help Israeli forces free other hostages if he was released, to keep track of time as the days slid by and be able to tell his family what happened to him. Now his body is free, but he cannot loosen those memories. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I was so out of control!’ Bez on cocaine, Happy Mondays, his ‘sexless marriage’ to Shaun Ryder, organic courgettes …
data.description: Drugs, drink and dancing made Bez famous. Thirty-five years on, has he really swapped it all for filtered water, intermittent fasting and walks with the dogs? Bez has both shoelaces undone and it’s making me nervous. Out walking his dogs, we’re up and over barbed wire, across streams and over gates. We bash through brambles and skid down slopes. I’m becoming fixated on the perilously trailing laces of his trainers and why he hasn’t tripped over them. Can he be such a thrill-seeker that a dog walk can be turned into an hour of jeopardy? Of course he can. This is Bez, anarchic maraca-shaker, party person, the man Shaun Ryder, his Happy Mondays bandmate and partner in crime, says is a bad influence. Bez, whose real name is Mark Berry, has been in more scrapes than seems possible for one person. A small sample: knocking his teeth out in a motorbike crash at the age of 16, threatened with a gun when he and Ryder were trying to buy crack in New York, kidnapped and held hostage during another drug deal, smashing his body up in another motorbike crash in 1999 and then getting MRSA in hospital and ending up in a coma for a month. Continue reading...

data.title: Bel review – a tearful, heartbreaking tribute to a spellbinding singer
data.description: Beldina Odenyo was on the verge of stardom when she took her own life in 2021. In this beautiful documentary, her grief-stricken sister Leah attempts to finish her album – and her journey will make you cry again and again In 2021, the Kenyan-Scottish singer-songwriter Beldina Odenyo was on the brink of major stardom. That October, aged 31, she headlined a gig at Edinburgh’s Usher Hall, delivering an instantly legendary performance; barefoot, cloaked and bone-shaking in its intensity. Everyone in that concert hall knew they were witnessing something extraordinary that night. Two weeks later, Odenyo took her own life. This tender and grief-stricken documentary, which opens a year after her death, is directed with remarkable care by Louise Lockwood. What emerges is a sensitively drawn portrait of a visionary artist haunted by trauma, formed through her teenage video diaries, the words of those who loved her, the handful of exquisite songs she left behind – kept in a folder on her hard drive named “passable demos” – and the determination of her older sister, Leah McAleer, to keep her astonishing voice alive. A deeply painful venture that she understands is itself a product of her insurmountable grief. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Like swapping a Bentley for a Ferrari’: can the Harry Potter stage show survive being chopped in half?
data.description: After a phenomenal decade-long run, the Cursed Child two-parter is being pruned. Will it still work? Our writer swishes her cloak, levitates her luggage – and hops aboard the streamlined Hogwarts Express ‘Silencio!” Two dozen tank-topped and T-shirted figures fall quiet, and look expectantly at movement director Nuno Silva. “If you’ve got a cloak, accio it now …” With that summoning charm cast, broomsticks are stowed, wands holstered, suitcases grabbed. The Harry Potter and the Cursed Child rehearsal room – a creaky church hall whose Victorian wall clock gives a serendipitously Hogwarts flavour – is a near-permanent bustle of activity. A sound technician quickly re-sets cues on her laptop, a costume designer helps an actor into a suspiciously long pair of gloves. Associate director Nicola Samer is quietly running notes with a couple of the leads while the rest of the company preps for the next scene. Continue reading...

data.title: Poland’s ‘solidarity’ push for EU energy resilience in face of Russian aggression
data.description: In the second article in a series on the Polish economy, we look at how the country is forging closer ties with its neighbours Two miles off the coast of Gdańsk, the white steel piles of Poland’s first offshore gas terminal rise from the slate-grey Baltic. Installed at a height eight metres above the waves, the floating cranes and construction vessels here are on the frontline of Europe’s push for energy security. Since the taps were turned off on Russian gas after Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine four years ago, Poland has turned to the global energy market for supplies. But while conditions are far from ideal as the Middle East war drives oil and gas prices to stratospheric levels, strengthening the diversity of the country’s energy mix remains a top priority for Poland, its Baltic neighbours, and the EU at large. Continue reading...

Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital, a sedative, as Tennessee officials attempted to put her to death last Wednesday in a case that shocked many in America and created headlines around the world. She was set to be the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Continue reading...

data.title: A moment that changed me: I was heading for disaster on the Greek version of Strictly. Then instinct kicked in
data.description: I was gripped by fear, aching all over – and still recovering from cancer treatment. But Dancing With the Stars was a joyous celebration of survival It was an invitation I accepted in a moment of madness – and, over the next three months, regretted many times a day. I was in over my head, often with my heels literally over my head: I’d signed up to appear on the Greek version of Strictly Come Dancing . Dancing With the Stars, as it is called in Greece, follows the same format as its UK counterpart, with an identical studio, a matching shiny floor, even many of the same costumes that are hired out and circulated among the 70 or more international versions of the BBC show. Of course, it’s all in Greek – and in the season I took part in, Covid restrictions had been imposed, which intensified its strangeness. Continue reading...

data.title: Carrie review – the teenage hell-raiser’s glorious return couldn’t come at a better time
data.description: This witty, smart remake takes bullying and telekinetic violence to new extremes. Even the shower scene is more excruciating than the original The automatic response to the news that a stone-cold classic of any genre is to be remade is “Why?” In an accompanying letter to critics, the creator of the new TV series Carrie, Mike Flanagan, promises us that this was the first question he asked himself too when he was approached about the project. Why mess with perfection – in this case, the Brian De Palma horror film, based on and nearly eclipsing in terms of cultural currency Stephen King’s debut novel about a telekinetic teen, that has been gloriously shocking audiences for half a century? But it’s a far less necessary question than usual. Why remake Carrie, a story of teenage bullying, alienation and the vengeful violence it can fuel, for the modern age? Babe, look around! We’ve got the internet now. We’ve taken teenage bullying, alienation and the fuelling of vengeful violence to levels that De Palma and King, with all their vaunted capacity for darkness, could never have imagined! We are, to use a construction popular among the very youth of whom we are speaking, Carriemaxxing these days. The question is not why remake but quite why it has taken this long. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Men are a scam!’ The trials of Danielle Ponder, the lawyer turned singer rooting for a better world
data.description: After representing society’s dispossessed, Ponder started a music career in her 40s – then faced miscarriage, anxiety and more. She explains her survival instinct “You can get everything you dreamed of career-wise, and your life can still crumble, and that is what happened to me,” says US singer-songwriter Danielle Ponder. Five years ago, and five days before her 40th birthday, Ponder left her job as a public defender – a lawyer for those without the means to pay for one – to pursue music full-time. Ponder’s rich, church-reared voice and resonant music quickly lent themselves to cinematic moments: she wrote and performed the theme song for Apple TV+’s Manhunt and her trip-hop-infused track Roll the Credits has been used by adverts, TV shows and video games. Several comments on the YouTube video come from viewers who searched for it thinking she was Nina Simone. Her debut album, Some of Us Are Brave, came out in 2022 and was warmly received by critics, and she appeared on Seth Meyers’ talkshow. Her gamble had paid off. “But personally,” she says, “it felt like everything around me was falling apart”. Continue reading...

data.title: Goodbye Warner, hello Skydance: how will the major merger really impact Hollywood?
data.description: After a windier road than expected, Paramount and Warner are now one, under the banner of Skydance, and the film industry is set for a shake-up Hollywood’s big five have officially become the big four. Following a twist-filled saga that saw century-old studio Warner Bros nearly acquired by streaming giant Netflix, only to be outbid by Paramount owners Skydance, the company led by billionaire scion David Ellison, then faced with legal opposition that ultimately crumbled, Warner Bros and Paramount are officially under the same corporate roof . They’re divisions of Skydance, which joins Sony, Disney and Universal as the remaining major-studio players in Hollywood. The merger goes beyond film production. Eventually, the streaming services HBO Max and Paramount+ will merge into a single entity, though a timeline has not been disclosed. The television channels HBO, Showtime, CBS, MTV, Comedy Central, Cartoon Network, Nickelodeon, TNT, TBS and CNN are among many now owned by a single corporation. The presence of CNN on that list has brought particular scrutiny, given the post-Skydance meddling with the once-respected CBS News, resulting in a rocky stewardship from Bari Weiss, who has overseen a dip in both ratings and prestige for the flagship program 60 Minutes. Weiss isn’t expected to add CNN to her purview; current chair Mark Thompson will remain in place for now , and Skydance has insisted that CNN will remain editorially independent. But given Ellison’s chumminess with Donald Trump, who has long ranted incoherently about CNN’s supposed biases, the presence of an oversight board with Ellison appointees has been cold comfort. Continue reading...

data.title: Three years on from the 7 October attacks, antisemitism has taken hold in Britain: Jews aren’t safe | Dave Rich
data.description: Britain cannot call itself a diverse democracy when communities are living with such fear. A line must be drawn. Let it be now On another anniversary of the 7 October attacks, the lasting impact on Britain’s Jews is found in the essential daily decisions we now have to make. Beyond the simple fear that you or your children might get killed the next time you go to synagogue or visit your local kosher shop, Jews are hiding the fact they are Jewish. This has gone beyond the choice of whether to wear your Star of David necklace inside or outside your shirt. It is found in the job applicants who remove their Jewish community volunteering from their CV; the people who use false names when ordering an Uber; the parents who move their children from mainstream schools to Jewish ones. Dave Rich is director of policy at the Community Security Trust. His new book , From Be’eri to Bondi: Global Antisemitism After October 7, is published by Routledge Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Why do billionaires have so many children if they’re not prepared to parent them? | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: Kim Kardashian’s revelation that she has five nannies for four children caused a ruckus. But the world of the ultra-wealthy throws up far more extreme approaches to childcare “I have the best advice for women in business,” Kim Kardashian told Variety in 2022 . “Get your fucking ass up and work. It seems like nobody wants to work these days.” The billionaire got a lot of flak for this comment but no one can accuse her of being a hypocrite. It takes serious graft to spin a sex tape into lasting fame and a business empire. That said, like many high-flyers who preach the importance of hard work, the Skims co-founder isn’t above outsourcing the less glamorous domestic labour. She has primary custody of the four kids she shares with her ex-husband, Kanye West, and, according to an interview with the Sunday Times , employs five nannies to take care of them: “One nanny on duty, four on rotation,” she said. Despite having more nannies than kids, she apparently still does the school run. And I bet she doesn’t turn up at the school gate with yoghurt on her shirt like I do. Continue reading...

data.title: Zack Polanski had the chance to show real leadership. He blew it | Rafael Behr
data.description: A toxic debate over anti-Zionism leaves the Green leader looking like a passenger in the movement that carried him to the top When Donald Trump calls someone a socialist he is not using the word in the same way that, say, Zohran Mamdani does. The mayor of New York espouses democratic socialism as a mission of equitable distribution of wealth and opportunity. The US president says socialism only pretends to be democratic “because it sounds so nice”; that “it’s really communism you’re talking about” and that people such as Mamdani pose “the biggest threat to our nation … since its founding”. People who despise an idea, seeing it as the manifestation of everything wicked, cannot be expected to define it accurately. As with the radical right and socialism, so it is with the left and Zionism. Rafael Behr is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Pedro Sánchez is a master of the political comeback. But calling a snap election in Spain may be a gamble too far | Paolo Gerbaudo
data.description: A thriving economy, a model green transition, social advances – Spain’s PM shouldn’t be in trouble. Yet he is, and it’s a lesson for progressives everywhere To progressives across the west, Spain has been a rare glimmer of hope in a world where far-right parties are increasingly entering government. Under Pedro Sánchez, who became prime minister in 2018, the country has combined a post-Covid economic boom with a bold green energy transition programme, and a pro-immigration stance with a principled opposition to the war agenda of Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu. Yet, at the end of next month, this rare beacon of democratic progress could fall. On Monday Sánchez called a snap general election , set for 29 November, after two decrees to address the country’s housing crisis were voted down in the lower chamber by politicians from rightwing parties. Speaking from the staircase of the Moncloa palace, Sánchez admitted that his government had not achieved all it had set out to do. “Many injustices remain to be corrected … particularly regarding inequality in public services and access to housing,” he said, adding: “To do more, we need to renew and expand public support.” Paolo Gerbaudo is a senior researcher at the faculty of political science and sociology of Complutense University in Madrid and a lead researcher at the Alameda Institute Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on the French school protests: the political class needs to heed the voice of students | Editorial
data.description: A generation facing unprecedented challenges deserves better than an underfunded education system One of the most famous slogans in France’s May 1968 student protests declared “ L’imagination au pouvoir ” (Power to the imagination). In a postwar context of steady growth, the ’68ers dreamed of shaping an egalitarian society, freed from the social constraints of their parents’ generation. Nearly five decades on, in a very different economic climate, the goal for most of the tens of thousands of pupils disrupting schools across the country is more modest. As one placard on display had it: “I’d like to be worrying about my maths exam, not my future”. A huge turnout of hundreds of thousands of protesters on Tuesday – a number that included many parents and teachers – confirmed the depth of resentment at years of budget cuts leading to crumbling school buildings, overcrowded classes and chronic staff shortages. Other complaints point to a lack of resources to deal with the now frequent heatwaves that make classrooms intolerable in May and June, and the unfairness of an opaque, algorithmically driven selection process for universities. data.title: Indonesia triumph in Infantino’s Asian brainchild but real impact could be votes
data.description: The inaugural Asean Cup, not to be confused with the existing Hyundai Asean Cup, may not live long in the memory but Fifa president sees benefit It’s probably not a coincidence, what with Fifa’s presidential election getting closer all the time, but Gianni Infantino has been sweeping through Asian member associations. There he was attending a ceremony in Macau to inaugurate new headquarters, signing an agreement in Mongolia to build a new national stadium and in Uzbekistan to open a Fifa Arena mini-pitch. All wise moves as Asia is still divided when it comes to the battle for the biggest job in world football. A number of associations have expressed support for the incumbent; others have openly opposed him; some will decide upon seeing the other candidate; some will follow the lead of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) leadership and vote against Infantino; others will just wait. The culmination of Infantino’s trip were the two finals of the inaugural Fifa Asean Cup, a new tournament for south-east Asia and a few invited guests. In Saturday’s final of the Asean Challenge Cup, the second-tier event held in Hong Kong, Infantino was greeted with chants of “Fifa Mafia”, but 48 hours later in Indonesia for the main event the reception for the 56-year-old was a little warmer. Jakarta is already onside and did Infantino a huge favour by winning a tournament that was very much his brainchild. Continue reading...

data.title: Beautiful butterflies get more attention from the public – and from scientists
data.description: Research has shown that colourful and patterned species are the subject of more studies, and receive more conservation funding Large and beautiful butterflies attract far more attention than species that are smaller and dull. Now a new study has shown that this bias towards beauty results in the boring butterflies being overlooked in conservation programmes. To understand the link between beauty and conservation, researchers surveyed more than 21,000 people from more than 100 countries, asking them to look at photos of European butterflies and rate their beauty on a scale of 1 to 10 based on their first impression. The results, which are published in Current Biology , reveal that larger more colourful and patterned butterflies, like the yellow swallowtail, were consistently rated more attractive than the smaller, less conspicuous brownish species, such as the alpine grayling. That bias also extended into scientific research, with more studies on attractive species, and more funding and resource going into conservation of showier species. Continue reading...

data.title: Scottish film could steal The Jazz Singer’s crown as ‘world’s first talkie’

The service will be tested in Spain and Portugal before the end of December and will be launched in the UK if it proves successful. Ikea already offers buy-back in stores, including in the UK. The online version will extend it to a much wider audience, with Ikea predicting pre-owned goods are likely to grab 16% of the UK homewares market by next year Continue reading...

data.title: Eva Marie Saint: the Hitchcock Blonde who outgrew the persona
data.description: Her glacial poise in North By Northwest made her a cinematic icon, but films including On the Waterfront and Loving revealed great subtlety alongside the glamour Eva Marie Saint dies aged 102 Her best films – ranked Her life in pictures ‘I’m Eve Kendall. I’m 26 and unmarried. Now you know everything.” Not quite everything. That is the famously succinct introduction given in a swaying dining car in a voice creamy with insinuation. Eve is speaking to Cary Grant’s fugitive ad man Roger Thornhill, wrongly accused of murder and hiding out from the cops on a train from New York to Chicago in Alfred Hitchcock’s 1959 classic North By Northwest. Eve is going to hide him in her compartment because she wants to have sex with him, and much later that train of theirs is to symbolically enter a tunnel. But is that the whole story? Eve’s amazingly beautiful, enigmatic face encodes a secret. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘My first photographs coincided with me falling in love’: why children have always adored taking pictures
data.description: What makes someone pick up a camera at a young age, and what can their images tell us? A new book and show explore why a child’s first photo could be as formative as their first record What was the first photograph you took? Though most of us use cameraphones every day, few think about how the habit started or even why we choose the pictures we keep. Photography is one of the most popular hobbies in the world, typically picked up in childhood, but its impact – particularly pre-smartphone and digital imagery – has not been much studied. This lapse fascinates Annebella Pollen, professor of visual and material culture at the University of Brighton. “My generation is used to being asked: ‘What was the first record you bought?’ Music is seen as a key part of identity formation, but what if something similar crystallises when we handle a camera?” she asks. “I certainly remember my first photos, because they coincided with me falling in love, as a 10-year-old, with a beautiful boy at school. I pursued him with my camera.” Continue reading...

data.title: Artificial review – Luca Guadagnino takes on OpenAI in muddled tech satire
data.description: New York film festival: The origin story of Sam Altman’s company is reimagined as a campy comedy starring Andrew Garfield On the day that Luca Guadagnino ’s film about Sam Altman and OpenAI premiered, Vanity Fair released a cover story on Altman. Alongside glossy portraits from Annie Leibovitz, the world’s pre-eminent portrait photographer, the story describes him as the Oppenheimer of his day, evoking the image of a man leading humanity towards its own inevitable demise at the hands of sentient robots. Altman doesn’t seem to be grappling with much existential angst about the whole thing though: in an interview also released this week, he said that we should be prepared to accept “bad things” in return for the benefits of AI. How much worse can things get? AI agents have already gone rogue , hacking into government systems and “bruteforcing” UN databases. Last year , a young woman used ChatGPT as a therapist before she killed herself (the software helped her write her suicide note). Studies show that using AI is probably leading us all towards something called cognitive surrender, which does not seem like the best use of your one wild and precious life. Continue reading...

data.title: 24 Hour Party People review – daring metatextual paean to the Manchester music scene
data.description: Rereleased for its 24th anniversary, Michael Winterbottom’s freewheeling film about a journalist who championed post-punk bands couldn’t have starred anyone but Steve Coogan Michael Winterbottom’s intriguing, daring, freewheeling movie is being rereleased for its 24th anniversary. It is about Manchester legend, Factory Records impresario, club owner and Granada TV journalist Tony Wilson, played by Steve Coogan, who was a driving entrepreneurial force behind the city’s music scene and guide to bands such as Joy Division, New Order and Happy Mondays. Looking back to my original review I see that I was in some ways unconvinced, perhaps by the almost flippant, throwaway tone that is somehow evenly established from first to last, with Coogan’s Partridgean lead performance – very good though it undoubtedly is – delivering all the lines as if doing a wry piece to camera. He was arguably the only possible casting for a minor TV personality who was also a major player in the real world beyond the camera, a postmodern combination that Wilson, a sophisticated and intelligent man, himself surely savoured. Winterbottom’s A Cock and Bull Story , adapted from Laurence Sterne, is sometimes described as his postmodern work, although this film, with its fourth-wall breaking, real-world cameos and docu-realist sense of itself, is probably even more metatextual. Continue reading...

data.title: Hamlet’s goodbye, the last of Leigh, Birmingham blues and a vampire in Vienna: 12 great films at the London film festival
data.description: Our critic picks out some of the most outstanding cinema screening at the UK’s most prestigious film event in 2026 This film puts Andrew Scott in line to become the first out gay man to win the best actor Oscar . He plays Ian Charleson, who became a star in Chariots of Fire and in 1989 took on the role of Hamlet at London’s National Theatre when Daniel Day-Lewis withdrew, despite being desperately ill with Aids, knowing that the strain would accelerate his illness. For Charleson, the play’s themes of life and death, truth and falsehood, justice and injustice, were all too real. Continue reading...

data.title: Blockers by Michael Lewis review – the quiet heroes who tried to stop Doge
data.description: The author of Moneyball brings his exceptional narrative skills to bear on Musk’s anti-government crusade Donald Trump’s catastrophic errors get so much attention that his systemic ones can easily be missed. While the world looks on in dismay at his farcical war in Iran, the thuggery of Ice agents or clownish attacks on erstwhile allies like Canada and Denmark, the core functions of the American government are slowly disintegrating. It is harder to get people to focus on the machinery of the state because the effects are often slow and hard to pin down. Outbreaks of disease – such as the recent wave of explosive diarrhoea across the US – might have happened anyway, but were probably made worse by lay-offs at the Centers for Disease Control. Likewise, Trump is not directly responsible for natural disasters, but response times in the past year may have been hampered by mass redundancies at the National Weather Service. Cuts to tax collection also seem to have reduced revenue by multiple billions, though we cannot be sure of the causal relationship. Continue reading...

data.title: Other Worlds Than These by Stephen King and Peter Straub review – a self-indulgent finale to the Talisman trilogy
data.description: There are moments of shivering joy as the protagonist of two enduring classics, Jack Sawyer, returns – but this time his journey feels endlessly repetitive Bear with me, because there is some backstory to get through before we can talk about the book I am actually here to review. Back in 1984, Stephen King and Peter Straub collaborated on the fantasy novel The Talisman. Like all the best King stories, it follows a young boy: in this case Jack Sawyer, 12, whose mother, Lily, is dying. Jack learns that a magical object called the Talisman might save her – if he can find it in a parallel world known as the Territories. Straub and King followed this up in 2001 with Black House , in which an adult Jack investigates a series of child murders that turn out to have disturbing links to the Territories. The books are very different: one a coming-of-age cross-country quest, in which Jack flips back and forth between two versions of the US; the other a fantastical and horror-inflected murder mystery. Both are brilliant and enduring classics which will always have a place on my bookshelves – I reread both of them, all 1,800-odd pages, to prepare for Other Worlds Than These and was as swept away and delighted as the first time round. Continue reading...

data.title: Silver Pines review – a stylish, neo-noir detective drama
data.description: PC, PS5, Switch 2; Wych Elm Games, Team 17 Abandoned shops, ruined apartment buildings and rotting sewer networks make up a dark landscape in which you play a private eye searching for a missing singer-songwriter In a weird deserted town miles from anywhere, a troubled detective searches for a missing musician and the girl he may or may not have murdered. It could be a Silent Hill game or a lost David Lynch movie from the 1990s – in fact, it’s neither. And also both. If that whets your appetite, stick around, there’s plenty more to come. Developed by Scandinavian studio Wych Elm Games, Silver Pines is a dark Metroidvania-style adventure, where you play as shambling private eye, Red Walker, exploring a 2D universe of abandoned shops, ruined apartment buildings and rotting sewer networks. Officially, everyone has left because of an incoming storm, but very quickly you learn that something much darker is afoot. Someone has hired you to find singer-songwriter Eddie Velvet, but you don’t know why; your only contact with your client is via the payphones dotted around town, where you can also save your progress – as long as you have a dollar to pay for the call. Each location is filled with clues and puzzles – a weird newspaper story pinned to the wall, a strange statue that needs a missing piece – and through these artefacts you unlock new rooms and descend further into the mystery. Continue reading...

data.title: Post your questions for Celia Imrie
data.description: From Miss Babs in Acorn Antiques to Calendar Girls, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel and her infamous appearance on The Celebrity Traitors, it’s hard to know where to begin Celia Imrie has had such a varied career, it’s hard to know where you might know her best from. Maybe it’s as Miss Babs, the permanently flustered antiques-shop owner in Victoria Wood’s Acorn Antiques, or as Philippa Moorcroft, Dinnerladies’ spectacularly uptight HR manager. Perhaps it’s as Bridget Jones’s family friend Una Alconbury, or from Calendar Girls, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel films, Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again. Maybe you know her as Mrs Quickly, the ghastly would-be stepmother in Nanny McPhee. Or maybe you first encountered her in Upstairs, Downstairs, To the Manor Born, Bergerac, Lovejoy or The Darling Buds of May, or as Claudia Bing, the magnificently awful PR rival of Jennifer Saunders’ Edina in Absolutely Fabulous. data.title: Women behind the lens: ‘I felt suspended between hope and giving up’
data.description: The Ethiopian photographer Sosina Mengistu’s self-portraits draw on personal experience to reflect young people’s anxiety and frustration This self-portrait is part of my project So I See Me, which I began in 2020 during the Covid-19 pandemic and continue to this day. The title reflects the central idea: using the camera to look at myself. But it also carries a subtle echo of my name, Sosina. When the pandemic started, I was in my final year of an engineering degree at the University of Gondar in Ethiopia. I was excited to graduate and begin the next chapter of my life, then everything suddenly came to a halt. Thinking the travel restrictions would only last for a short time, I decided to stay with my uncle in Bahir Dar in the north rather than travel back to my home town, Asosa, more than 450 miles to the west. I ended up stuck there for eight months. Continue reading...

data.title: Who owns ‘brain rot’? Inside the international legal drama over a beloved meme
data.description: Copyright law in the US only applies to human-made creations, but AI characters like Tung Tung Tung Sahur are challenging that One of the most beloved characters in an absurdist genre of online video content has become the center of an international legal battle that could determine where human creativity ends and artificial intelligence begins. Tung Tung Tung Sahur, also known as Triple T, was created in 2025 by an Indonesian teen who goes by the username Noxa, using OpenAI’s image-generation tool. Based on a kentongan – a type of drum used to wake south-east Asian Muslims for their pre-dawn meal during Ramadan – the character is an anthropomorphized version of the instrument with a broad smile and a vacant stare. He sits under the umbrella of “Italian brain rot” internet videos. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s hard to imagine the fires of July’: a bike ride through the Cairngorms in Scotland
data.description: Wildfires raged through the national park this summer, but much of the landscape remains untouched – and autumn is the perfect time to go In the Cairngorms national park, the bracken is changing from dark green to russet and umber. Birch leaves are lined with gold, while the Scots pines remain proudly green. Autumn is arriving with a little sigh of relief here, after a summer few will forget. The wildfire that began near Glenmore and Abernethy on 15 July burned more than 33 sq km (13 sq miles) of moorland and forest. More than 500 firefighters were involved; homes and businesses were evacuated; and the emergency response lasted over a month. Visiting now, it’s hard to see, or even imagine, the damage. Much of the burned area is high on the hill and far from the roads. It’s a huge loss but, in a national park stretching 4,528 sq km (1,748 sq miles), surprisingly easy to miss. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘We live in grief-phobic societies’: experts on how to get more comfortable with death
data.description: We are all going to die, and so is everyone we know. So how can you not be terrified? For most people, death is not a standard conversation topic. Once, at lunch, a friend began talking about her mother’s death several years earlier. Her voice caught occasionally, but she spoke about it plainly – like a simple fact of life. As we talked, I noticed another friend was shifting uncomfortably in his seat; he didn’t say much. Afterwards, I asked him what was wrong. “I really don’t like talking about death,” he said, his hands twitching anxiously. “I don’t even like thinking about it. It freaks me out.” Continue reading...

data.title: Roast chicken, congee and cookies: Ravinder Bhogal’s autumn squash recipes
data.description: Nutty in flavour and creamy in texture, autumn’s bounty of squash and pumpkin has many uses, both sweet and savoury The shops are heaving with pumpkins and squash, and though there are so many different varieties to choose from, most of them are interchangeable. My favourites are kabocha, crown prince and delicata, for their deeply nutty flavour and creamy texture, plus they hold their shape well when roasted or braised. And if you’re carving a pumpkin for Halloween over the coming weeks, don’t waste the flesh: chop it up and throw into a risotto. It’s hard to imagine that such deliciousness could come from such a ghoulish grimace. Continue reading...

data.title: How to maximise the umami in mushrooms | Kitchen aide
data.description: Whether you sizzle, sweat, wet-fry or oven-cook, enhancing the savoury flavour of your mushrooms will depend on the variety, says our panel of fun guys How do I cook mushrooms at home so they have th e umami you get in restaurant dishes? John, by email For Chantelle Nicholson, chef-patron of Apricity in London, boosting the savoury side of ’shrooms comes down to three main things. First, they hold a lot of water, so “you need to cook that out of them, so heat is super-important, as are fat and salt”. Tomás Gormley, chef-owner of Cardinal in Edinburgh, adds that he can “almost guarantee” that John isn’t using enough of the latter: “As a rule, I use 1.5% of the weight of whatever I’m seasoning. With mushrooms, especially, season early, before they hit the pan, to draw out their moisture. That resulting mushroomy water then cooks the mushrooms while it’s reducing and concentrating the flavour.” But there are so many varieties of mushrooms out there, and they all behave in different ways, so John needs to be using the right ones for the job. “If you’re making a soup, puree or paté, field, portobello or button mushrooms are fine,” Nicholson says. “But if you’re looking for a delicious sauteed mushroom, say, ideally you need something with less water content – chestnut, shiitake or blue/grey oyster mushrooms. Heat oil in a pan, then add the shredded or sliced mushrooms, and season with fine salt straight away.” Nicholson would be inclined to toss in a bay leaf and some thyme or sage, too, and maybe a smashed clove of garlic. “Cook over a high-ish heat until lightly golden, then add a bit of butter and keep cooking until golden. If you want to enhance the flavour even further, a splash of dry sherry works really well.” Got a culinary dilemma? Email feast@theguardian.com Continue reading...

data.title: Alice Zaslavsky’s shortcut beetroot baked risotto – recipe
data.description: An unconventional technique makes this vibrant rice – finished with dill fronds – a lower-touch dinner for weeknights Check out more Alice Zaslavsky recipes This shortcut risotto will have purists shaking their fists, but I like to live dangerously. Unlike traditional risottos where you stir the whole time, this one gets bunged in the oven with all its liquid, then right at the end, use a whisk to release the starches for a creamy finish. Use a microplane to grate the parmesan over the risotto. This will yield a cloud-like consistency, but you could also just blitz the parmesan to a crumb in the food processor before grating the veg. I’d avoid buying pre‑grated parmesan, as it’s kept crumby with anti-caking agent, and the aroma is … not great. Continue reading...

data.title: NGOs say Israel bombed a journalist and appeared to attack ambulances trying to aid her – explainer
data.description: Journalist Amal Khalil was killed in April in what colleagues described as a sustained attack by Israeli forces. Rescuers attempted to dig her out of the rubble of a building that had been targeted by Israeli forces, who had also prevented them from providing life-saving assistance. Beirut-based Guardian correspondent Will Christou explains how investigations by Human Rights Watch (HRW), Amnesty International and Legal Agenda show that Israel deliberately and directly attacked Khalil and her colleague Zeinab Faraj, with apparent knowledge that they were journalists. The organisations called for the attacks to be investigated as war crimes, while HRW called for states to halt arms sales to Israel and put targeted sanctions on Israeli officials responsible for ongoing crimes. Deliberately attacking journalists is a war crime. Israel has killed at least 15 journalists in Lebanon and 210 in Gaza since 2023, according to the UN human rights office . Israel said it 'regrets any harm caused to journalists', and that they were killed 'as part of a series of events' during which two Hezbollah military operatives were killed Israeli strike that killed journalist in Lebanon was war crime, say rights groups Continue reading...

data.title: How dilapidated are French schools and how bad is inequality in the education system?

data.title: California couple say they spent $300,000 fixing alleged county damage, then got $676,703 bill
data.description: A California couple says Santa Clara County entered their property to address a landslide threatening a public road, left the hillside damaged and later billed them $676,703.22 for the work. The couple says it spent more than $300,000 repairing hazardous conditions allegedly caused by the county. A federal judge has now dismissed their current complaint but allowed them to amend several constitutional claims, keeping part of the legal battle alive.

data.title: Ron Burkle bought Frank Lloyd Wright’s Ennis House for $4.5M, restored it, then sold it for $18M
data.description: Billionaire investor Ron Burkle acquired the iconic Ennis House, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, at a bargain due to its deteriorated state. After pouring approximately $17 million into comprehensive renovations, the property was exquisitely restored and listed for $18 million in 2024. This impressive sale established a new benchmark for architecturally significant homes, underscoring the importance of conserving historic structures for future appreciation.

data.title: Après l’attaque déjouée de Fairford, au Royaume-Uni, les bases aériennes françaises se préparent à la « guerre hybride »
data.description: En France, du 28 septembre au 2 octobre, toutes les bases aériennes se sont entraînées à limiter leur vulnérabilité face aux risques d’attaques de drones, d’intrusions ou de cyberattaques. data.title: L’Arabie saoudite, le Pakistan et la Turquie posent le premier acte de leur accord de défense mutuelle face aux houthistes
data.description: Mis en difficulté par les houthistes du Yémen, qui visent ses pétroliers et ses infrastructures, Riyad a activé lundi, avec ses deux alliés, le « pacte de La Mecque » conclu le 7 août. data.title: Nobel de Química 2026 vai para compreensão de como a natureza escolhe entre imagens espelhadas
data.description: O prêmio Nobel de Química de 2026 ficou com os pesquisadores Henri Kagan, da Universidade Paris-Sud, da França, e para Kenso Soai, da Universidade de Ciência de Tokyo, no Japão. O prêmio é pela descoberta de efeitos não lineares e da autocatálise na síntese orgânica assimétrica. Descoberta tem impacto em em medicamentos e também no entendimento de como a homoquiralidade -ou seja, o predomínio de um molécula espelhada sobre a outra- surgiu e ocorre na natureza. Leia mais (10/07/2026 - 06h51)

Com os melhores e mais frescos frutos do mar servidos no Rio . Esses são alguns dos comentários sobre o Satyricon feitos no boca a boca há décadas pelos cariocas. Uma reputação construída bem antes de as resenhas (publis ou espontâneas) existirem na internet. Logo na porta há um aviso sobre o dress code: proibido trajes de banho. Ou seja, nada de ir direto da praia . O ambiente é sóbrio e, antes de adentrar o salão, o comensal já tem ideia do que está por vir ao passar por um balcão com ostras e reluzentes pescados repousados sobre o gelo. Leia mais (10/06/2026 - 23h00)

data.title: O que pode uma mulher com a caneta nas mãos?
data.description: No Brasil, apenas 5,2% dos cargos de CEO são ocupados por mulheres . Chegar ao topo continua sendo raro , e ficar lá -de um jeito que produza mudança, não apenas presença- é um desafio para o qual poucas mulheres estão preparadas. Os cargos não vêm com manual. Vêm, no máximo, com uma pergunta silenciosa: o que fazer, na prática, com o poder que se tem em mãos? Leia mais (10/06/2026 - 22h00)

data.title: Nieuwe aanwas wolven in Nederland stabiliseert. ‘De topgebieden voor wolven in Nederland zijn nu wel bezet’
data.description: Het geboortecijfer van wolven in Nederland lijkt zich te stabiliseren. Dit jaar werden 56 wolvenwelpen geboren, bijna evenveel als vorig jaar (52). Dat betekent niet dat wolf zich niet verder zal uitbreiden in Nederland, zegt de onderzoeker. „Er zijn nu veertien roedels, maar er is ruimte voor minstens het dubbele.”

data.title: KOMENTÁŘ: Pusťte piráta za volant, dostanete osm let dopravního teroru
data.description: Pokud v posledních osmi letech sedáte za volant auta či jen do taxíku v Praze, nepotřebujete mezinárodní statistiky na to, abyste věděli, že situace je na zbláznění. Pro jistotu si stačí otevřít globální TomTom Traffic Index. Podle něj stráví Pražan ročně v zácpách 106 hodin. A když už se silnice města navečer uvolní, změní se pro změnu v závodní dráhu pro křápy na úvěr a rejdiště mopedistů se řvoucími výfuky.

data.title: Dvě děti nikdy nechodily do školy. Úřad je kvůli chybě vynechal ze seznamu
data.description: V případu dvou dětí, které nikdy nechodily do školy, aniž by si toho úřady všimly, chybovala obec při předávání seznamů dětí spádovým školám. Dětský ombudsman Martin Beneš o tom informoval na webu. Případ vyšel najevo až při zásahu policie a orgánu sociálně-právní ochrany dětí (OSPOD). Obecní úřad po šetření své postupy napravil. O jakou obec šlo, ombudsman neuvedl.

data.title: Macron z lodě sledoval test nové francouzské balistické střely, mluvil o odstrašení
data.description: Francie poprvé úspěšně otestovala novou balistickou střelu M51.3 schopnou nést jadernou hlavici. Test osobně sledoval francouzský prezident Emmanuel Macron.

data.title: Třicátá Ji.hlava nabídne filmy, co změnily svět. I dokument o pobodání Rushdieho

data.title: Kormoráni ohrožují ekosystémy střední Evropy, Červený žádá sousedy o spolupráci
data.description: Ministerstvo životního prostředí (MŽP) požádalo Polsko a Německo, aby přijaly opatření k regulaci populací kormorána velkého v oblastech u Severního a Baltského moře. Podle úřadu vysoký počet kormoránů způsobuje v České republice každoročně škody za desítky milionů korun. V zimním období jich na území Česka zůstává přibližně 12 000 až 14 000, další tisíce přes české území od podzimu do jara migrují.

data.title: Izrael si připomíná třetí výročí masakrů Hamásu. Trauma promluví i do voleb
data.description: Izraelci si připomínají třetí výročí útoků palestinské teroristické skupiny Hamás a jejích spojenců ze 7. října 2023. Po celém Izraeli se uskuteční vzpomínkové akce. Útoky, při nichž ozbrojenci zabili 1200 lidí a dalších 251 unesli do Pásma Gazy, byly nejkrvavější v izraelské historii. Izrael po nich v Gaze spustil odvetnou válku, v níž podle tamního ministerstva zdravotnictví zemřelo 74 tisíc lidí.

Proto jsme vyrazili s fotoaparátem zachytit krásný podzim před tím, že začnou plískanice.

data.title: Vražda matky a pokus o zabití otce. Obžalovali osmnáctiletou dívku a jejího přítele

data.title: Lukáši, proč lžeš? Na Praze 4 vře před volbami ostrá kampaň kvůli nájmu radnice
data.description: Jen několik dní před komunálními volbami se v Praze 4 rozhořel tuhý boj o zastupitelská křesla. data.title: Nová tarifní struktura bude férovější. Dřívější pokusy o změnu ztroskotaly, uvádí úřad
data.description: Inovace tarifní struktury u vysokého a velmi vysokého napětí začne platit už od 1. ledna příštího roku. Přípravy na tuto důležitou změnu v české energetice, která má do budoucna zamezit blokování kapacity v síti, tak nyní vrcholí. „Nově také platí povinnost uzavřít dodatek ke smlouvám o připojení do začátku listopadu,“ upozornili experti na tiskové konferenci Energetického regulačního úřadu a Svazu energetiky.

Přípravy na tuto důležitou změnu v české energetice, která má do budoucna zamezit blokování kapacity v síti, tak nyní vrcholí. „Nově také platí povinnost uzavřít dodatek ke smlouvám o připojení do začátku listopadu,“ upozornili experti na tiskové konferenci Energetického regulačního úřadu a Svazu energetiky.

data.title: Zadržený exšéf BND byl v kontaktu s agentem Ázerbájdžánu, píše magazín
data.description: Bývalý šéf německé rozvědky BND August Hanning, kterého v úterý pro podezření ze špionáže zadržela policie, podle německých vyšetřovatelů zřejmě udržoval kontakty s agentem z Ázerbájdžánu. Hanning je podezřelý, že si přes někdejšího vedoucího své kanceláře v BND Manfreda D. po odchodu ze zpravodajské služby za peníze obstarával tajné dokumenty, na základě kterých sestavil písemnou bezpečnostní analýzu.

data.title: 'One of the greats': Tupou signs off on Roosters career
data.description: Sydney, Australia Daniel Tupou evades Newcastle's Dane Gagai (left) and Dominic Young in the grand final. (Dan Himbrechts/ AAP PHOTOS ) By George Clarke in Sydney/ AAP Trent Robinson says Daniel Tupou will be remembered as one of the Sydney Roosters' all-time greats, after the four-time premiership-winning winger announced his retirement from the NRL . Tupou is ending his 15-year career on a high after helping the Roosters win Sunday's grand final against Newcastle. The 35-year-old, who had been coy about his future all season, became just the sixth player in Roosters history to win four premierships with the club. Across a 307-game, one-club career, the winger scored 198 tries, the third most of any player in premiership history behind Ken Irvine and Alex Johnston. " When you look at what Daniel Tupou has achieved over 15 seasons, he will stand as one of the greats," Robinson said in a statement. " But those numbers only tell part of the story of Toops and what he means to this club. " Since he made his debut, he has represented what we want a Rooster to be. " He has been incredibly consistent, selfless and dependable, and whenever there has been a big moment or a tough moment, he has been present. The Roosters' Daniel Tupou was renowned as a high-ball specialist. (Mark Evans/ AAP PHOTOS ) "Toops revolutionised the aerial game at the Sydney Roosters and became the greatest high-ball specialist of all time." Tupou's exit comes as the Roosters prepare for a big off-season exodus over the coming weeks. Fellow winger Mark Nawaqanitawase and back-rower Angus Crichton are moving to rugby union, Daly Cherry-Evans is heading to Super League side Hull FC , and Connor Watson is joining St George Illawarra. Daly Cherry-Evans and Daniel Tupou finished their time at the Roosters in triumphant fashion. (Mark Evans/ AAP PHOTOS ) But none of them get close to having the impact the towering winger has had on the Roosters since his NRL debut in 2012. As well as four premierships (2013, 2018, 2019, 2026), Tupou has won three World Club Challenges and played Test matches for both Tonga and Australia. He was part of the Tongan side that defeated the Kangaroos in 2019, in one of the biggest upsets in international rugby league history. Tupou played 10 times for NSW at State of Origin level between 2014 and 2022. " We love Toops, we're incredibly proud of him, and his name will always hold a very special place in the history of the Sydney Roosters," Robinson said. Tupou retires as the greatest try-scorer in Roosters history after surpassing Anthony Minichiello in 2023. Daniel Tupou holds the record for the most tries scored for the Sydney Roosters. data.translatedTitle: 'One of the greats': Tupou signs off on Roosters career
data.translatedDescription: Sydney, Australia Daniel Tupou evades Newcastle's Dane Gagai (left) and Dominic Young in the grand final. (Dan Himbrechts/ AAP PHOTOS ) By George Clarke in Sydney/ AAP Trent Robinson says Daniel Tupou will be remembered as one of the Sydney Roosters' all-time greats, after the four-time premiership-winning winger announced his retirement from the NRL . Tupou is ending his 15-year career on a high after helping the Roosters win Sunday's grand final against Newcastle. The 35-year-old, who had been coy about his future all season, became just the sixth player in Roosters history to win four premierships with the club. Across a 307-game, one-club career, the winger scored 198 tries, the third most of any player in premiership history behind Ken Irvine and Alex Johnston. " When you look at what Daniel Tupou has achieved over 15 seasons, he will stand as one of the greats," Robinson said in a statement. " But those numbers only tell part of the story of Toops and what he means to this club. " Since he made his debut, he has represented what we want a Rooster to be. " He has been incredibly consistent, selfless and dependable, and whenever there has been a big moment or a tough moment, he has been present. The Roosters' Daniel Tupou was renowned as a high-ball specialist. (Mark Evans/ AAP PHOTOS ) "Toops revolutionised the aerial game at the Sydney Roosters and became the greatest high-ball specialist of all time." Tupou's exit comes as the Roosters prepare for a big off-season exodus over the coming weeks. Fellow winger Mark Nawaqanitawase and back-rower Angus Crichton are moving to rugby union, Daly Cherry-Evans is heading to Super League side Hull FC , and Connor Watson is joining St George Illawarra. Daly Cherry-Evans and Daniel Tupou finished their time at the Roosters in triumphant fashion. (Mark Evans/ AAP PHOTOS ) But none of them get close to having the impact the towering winger has had on the Roosters since his NRL debut in 2012. As well as four premierships (2013, 2018, 2019, 2026), Tupou has won three World Club Challenges and played Test matches for both Tonga and Australia. He was part of the Tongan side that defeated the Kangaroos in 2019, in one of the biggest upsets in international rugby league history. Tupou played 10 times for NSW at State of Origin level between 2014 and 2022. " We love Toops, we're incredibly proud of him, and his name will always hold a very special place in the history of the Sydney Roosters," Robinson said. Tupou retires as the greatest try-scorer in Roosters history after surpassing Anthony Minichiello in 2023. Daniel Tupou holds the record for the most tries scored for the Sydney Roosters. (Dave Hunt/ AAP PHOTOS ) He has the second-most appearances for Easts, behind prop Jared Waerea-Hargreabes. " To have played my whole NRL career at one club means a lot to me," Tupou said. " The Roosters gave me my opportunity and this has become my home. " To play more than 300 games, win four premierships and share those moments with so many great teammates is something I'll always be proud of." data.title: La filière coton peine à retrouver son dynamisme en Ituri
data.description: Autrefois l’un des moteurs de l’économie dans la plaine du lac Albert, la culture du coton traverse aujourd’hui une période difficile en Ituri. Baisse de la production, difficultés d’écoulement, routes dégradées, manque d’encadrement des producteurs et arrêt de certaines unités de transformation freinent le développement de cette filière. À l’occasion de la Journée mondiale du coton, célébrée le 7 octobre, l’opérateur économique et ancien vice-gouverneur de l’Ituri, Pacifique Keta, appelle à relancer toute la chaîne de valeur.

data.title: Dégradation de la desserte en électricité en RDC
data.description: Depuis plusieurs semaines, la fourniture d’électricité se dégrade à Kinshasa et dans plusieurs villes du pays. Dans la capitale, des habitants de plusieurs quartiers affirment subir des coupures qui durent parfois plusieurs semaines, voire plusieurs mois. Sur les réseaux sociaux, les témoignages se multiplient pour dénoncer les conséquences de ces interruptions sur la vie quotidienne, les activités économiques et la sécurité dans les quartiers plongés dans l’obscurité.

data.title: Lancement d’une campagne de sensibilisation à la paix et au vivre-ensemble à Djugu
data.description: Une campagne de sensibilisation à la paix a été lancée lundi 5 octobre dans le territoire de Djugu, en province de l’Ituri, à l’initiative du chef du secteur de Walendu Djatsi. Le lancement officiel a eu lieu à Djugu-Centre lors d’un meeting réunissant les différentes communautés locales. À cette occasion, sa majesté Justin Gudza Kiza a appelé les populations à privilégier le vivre-ensemble, le pardon et l’acceptation mutuelle afin de consolider une paix durable dans la région.

data.title: THE LAW 101: Trial in Absentia -the law exists, but where are the rules?
data.description:
I have just read Oliver Barker-Vormawor’s very educative 41-paragraph piece on the calls for the OSP to simply put former Finance Minister Ken Ofori-Atta on trial in absentia. I have little useful to add to his central argument. But his intervention confirms concerns I have raised about how quickly sections of the media have embraced the refrain, “just try him in absentia,” without sufficient attention to the important nuances of our law. Let me try explaining in the next 24 paragraphs.

Yes, our law recognises trial in absentia. But that is only the beginning of the inquiry. How exactly is such a trial commenced and conducted where the accused was already outside Ghana when proceedings began, has never appeared before the trial court (I do not know of one) and has never personally been arraigned? I am searching for a precedent.

data.title: THE LAW 101: Before you fly that drone
data.description:
The arrest of three persons for allegedly flying drones over the EOCO headquarters is a useful reminder: owning a drone does not give you an unrestricted right to fly it wherever you please.

Ghana regulates drones, legally, Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS), principally under the Ghana Civil Aviation Act, 2024 (Act 1120) and the Ghana Civil Aviation (RPAS) Directives, 2018, Part 28.

The rules begin even before take-off. Prior GCAA approval is required to import, export, sell or operate a drone or its parts. The drone must be registered, and registration alone is not permission to fly. Part 28.7 is emphatic: “No person shall fly an RPAS without a Permit issued by the Authority.”

data.title: The only thing that flows regularly is THE BILL
data.description:
Perhaps there is a perfectly reasonable explanation for every cedi on my bill. Excellent.

Then show me the opening meter reading, the closing meter reading, the units consumed, the tariff applied and whether the bill is based on an actual reading or an estimate.

That should not require a pilgrimage to PURC.

Because electricity billing should be arithmetic.

It should not require revelation.

It may be about who is holding the remote control.

data.title: Transparence budgétaire : Madagascar progresse mais reste encore loin du compte
data.description: Madagascar progresse légèrement en matière de transparence budgétaire, mais reste encore loin du niveau jugé satisfaisant. Les résultats de l'Enquête sur le budget ouvert (EBO) 2025, réalisée par MSIS Tatao, et présentée mardi 6 octobre, font apparaître des insuffisances importantes, aussi bien dans l'accès aux informations que dans la participation citoyenne et le contrôle des finances publiques. La transparence budgétaire obtient une note de 44/100, contre 39/100 lors de la précédente (…) - Economie

data.title: Cuando el cáncer de mama cambia el cuerpo pero no la vida
data.description: En Costa Rica, el cáncer de mama encabeza los diagnósticos de tumores malignos entre las mujeres y cada año se registran más de 1.300 nuevos casos. Datos de la CCSS señalan que una de cada 20 mujeres podría enfrentar este diagnóstico a lo largo de su vida. Este reportaje reúne las historias de cuatro sobrevivientes, las claves de prevención y detección temprana explicadas por una ginecóloga oncóloga y las opciones de reconstrucción mamaria después del cáncer desde el criterio de un cirujano plástico con especialización en reconstrucción de senos.

data.title: Messi se va de Argentina con emotivo discurso y se acuerda de su padre: "El día más triste de mi carrera"
data.description: Lionel Messi afirmó este martes que "fue un orgullo muy grande defender esta camiseta" y que "jugar en la selección Argentina es lo más lindo que te puede pasar", tras la victoria de este martes por 3-0 con un gol suyo ante Benín en su último partido con la Albiceleste, jugado en el estadio Monumental de Buenos Aires. "Fue un orgullo muy grande defender esta camiseta en estos más de 20 años, hasta en los peores momentos nunca dejé de luchar y de dar el máximo", dijo el goleador histórico de la Albiceleste ante una multitud emocionada. "El no venir más va a ser un dolor muy grande. Les juro que me gustaría venir toda la vida porque jugar en la selección Argentina es lo más lindo que te puede pasar", agregó, en un mensaje en el centro del campo y rodeado por la plantilla celeste y blanca y su familia. Messi hizo una sentida referencia a su padre, Jorge Messi, fallecido poco tiempo después de finalizado el Mundial 2026 , en el que Argentina fue finalista. "Siento que es el momento, en el último Mundial fue demasiado todo lo que me tocó vivir. Tuvimos el sueño mío y de todo el país de volver a ser campeones del mundo, estuvimos muy cerquita", dijo Messi y los fanáticos lo ovacionaron al grito de "Dale, campeón". Relató que el partido contra Inglaterra por las semifinales del Mundial 2026 fue un "desgaste muy grande a nivel de piernas y emocional. Llegamos muy justo, la peleamos". "No tengan dudas de que los compañeros que tuve al lado siempre dejaron todo por esta camiseta", expresó el astro, y les agradeció por "cumplirles el sueño de chiquito" de ganar títulos con la selección nacional. "Tenía guerreros al lado que sabía que dejaban la vida", los describió. En un diálogo constante con el público que lo ovacionaba, dijo: "Voy a extrañar muchísimo jugar acá, tuve la suerte de jugar por todo el país y siempre recibí el cariño de todos. Soy un agradecido por lo que me tocó vivir. Siempre la cancha llena, estuvieron en todos lados. Sabemos el esfuerzo que hacen. Siempre somos locales en todos lados y eso lo sentimos". "Los voy a extrañar y ahora voy a estar de ese lado, bancando a estos chicos y a los que vengan. Siempre unidos. Quedó demostrado que cuando nos juntamos y estamos unidos somos más fuertes que cualquiera y superamos lo que sea", dijo Messi, y pidió apoyo al futuro de la Selección. "Hay gente que quiere ver mal a la selección y no hay que darles el gusto", subrayó. "Estoy orgulloso de ser argentino y haber cumplido el sueño con todos ustedes. Los quiero", concluyó el atacante de 39 años, envuelto en el canto de la gente. "Es difícil decir algo hoy. Hay muchas emociones, muchas cosas... obviamente en lo primero que pienso es en mi viejo. No me queda más que agradecer. Fue un orgullo muy grande defender esta camiseta, hasta en los peores momentos. Nunca dejé de luchar, de pelear, de dar el máximo y de querer estar siempre. No venir más va a ser un dolor muy grande, Les juro que me gustaría venir toda la vida porque jugar en la selección argentina es lo más lindo que te puede pasar". "Como dije, si bien quiero estar acá toda la vida, siento que es el momento. El último Mundial ya fue demasiado todo lo que me tocó vivir. Tuvimos el sueño de volver a ser campeones del mundo. El mío y el de todo un país. El último Mundial estuvimos cerquita. No pasó nada raro, es la realidad, como se dice. El partido de Inglaterra fue un desgaste muy grande (Y le cortan porque se pone todo el estadio a botar). A nivel de piernas y emocional fue un desgaste muy grande. Llegamos con lo justo pero lo peleamos como siempre. No pudimos ser campeones. Todos los compañeros que tuve al lado siempre dejaron todo por esta camiseta, siempre". "Agradecer a mis compañeros por este tiempo, por lo que compartí con este grupo. Me hicieron ser campeones del mundo, de América, Finalissima y todo lo que jugamos. Fue un orgullo enorme para mí compartir dentro y fuera de la cancha con todos ellos. Competíamos a cualquiera porque sabñía que tenía guerreros al lado que se dejaban la vida. Seguramente me olvido de muchas cosas que me gustaría decirles. Es un momento muy difícil para mí. Voy a extrañar muchísimo jugar acá. Siempre recibí un cariño enorma, de principio a fin. Soy un agradecido por todo lo que me tocó vivir". "Agradezco todo este tiempo que siempre, fui donde fui, la cancha llena, sea el partido que sea. Mundiales, Copa América... haciendo un esfuerzo enorme. Ustedes siempre lo hacen. Siempre somos locales en todos lados. Y nosotros lo sentimos". "Me tocó vivir uno de los días más felices de mi carrera. Fue cuando volvimos a jugar después de ganar el Mundial. Fue lo más lindo que me pasó. Fue hermoso. Hasta día de hoy veo videos y me emocionó. Quedará en la historia de todos nosotros. Muchísimas gracias". "Hoy me toca vivir seguramente el día más triste de mi carrera. Le digo adiós a todos ustedes, a la selección. Ahora voy a estar de ese lado, bancando a estos chicos y a todos los que vengan. Siempre unidos".

data.title: Messi cierra su ciclo en Argentina como el mejor: gol y dos asistencia en su despedida
data.description: El 3-0 de Argentina a Benín , el gol de penal de Lionel Messi , sus asistencias para dos más y un legado de 126 tantos en 21 años de historia con la Selección Albiceleste sumaron en una noche en Buenos Aires a una jornada que comenzó con emoción y terminó con lágrimas. La Selección de Argentina debió esperar al segundo tiempo para doblegar a un duro rival, que solo sucumbió tras los golpes asestados por Nicolás Otamedi (m.48) a una asistencia de Messi tras un córner, el golazo de Nico Paz (m.61) a pase del astro y por fin el tanto suyo de penalti (m.70). El partido jugado en el estadio Monumental Antonio Vespucio Liberti de Buenos Aires fue seguido por unos 85.000 espectadores. El encuentro estuvo marcado por la entrada en calor de Argentina con el foco puesto en Lionel Messi que, en su ingreso saludó a las cuatro tribunas de un estadio Monumental colmado. Luego en el ingreso del equipo, el capitán de 39 años estuvo acompañado por sus tres hijos Thiago, Mateo y Ciro , mientras que tuvo en el himno su primer momento de casi lágrimas, mientras una bandera en forma de camiseta con el ‘Gracias Messi’ ocupaba gran parte del campo de juego. En el encuentro, Messi se mostró activo en su zona preferida del campo de juego, desde la izquierda al centro del campo. Dos asistencias de lujo a Lautaro Martínez y Agustín Giay encontraron al portero Marcel Dandijnou con buenas respuestas, al igual que un tiro libre del propio Leo que controló el portero del conjunto africano. Al promediar el partido Messi recibió un pase al vacío de su amigo y compañero de Inter Miami, Rodrigo De Paul , y su anticipo a Dandijnou se fue apenas desviado, mientras que un tiro de esquina cerrado también encontró una buena respuesta del dorsal dos de Benín. La visita tuvo sus opciones para sorprender e irse en ventaja pero un error en definición de Aiyegun Tosin y dos intervenciones de Emiliano Martínez dejaron el cero para irse al descanso. En el segundo tiempo, Argentina golpeó rápidamente en el minuto 51 con un tiro de esquina de Lionel Messi que conectó Nicolás Otamendi para convertir en su despedida de la Selección Argentina . El segundo llegó con una asistencia de Messi para una definición exquisita del recién ingresado Nico Paz en el minuto 61 que dejó sin reacción al portero Marcel Dandijinou. Luego un penalti marcado por una infracción en el área derivó en el gol del gran homenajeado de la noche que tomó la pelota y definió con un toque a la izquierda del portero de Benín para su gol número 126 con la casaca de la Selección... el último. Sobre el final le quedó un tiro libre que se fue por arriba del travesaño para que luego el chileno Fernando Vejar marque el final del partido y sentencie el final de la era Messi en la Selección Argentina . 3.⁠ ⁠Argentina: Emiliano Martínez; Agustín Giay, Cristian Romero (m.79, Giovani Lo Celso), Nicolás Otamendi (m.51, Lisandro Martínez), Nicolás Tagliafico (m.51, Facundo Medina); Rodrigo De Paul (m.58, Nicolás González), Alexis Mac Allister (m.79, Franco Mastantuono), Enzo Fernández (m.79, Exequiel Palacios); Lionel Messi; Julián Álvarez (m.58, Nicolás Paz) y Lautaro Martínez (m.79, Leonel Flores). Seleccinoador: Lionel Scaloni. 0.⁠ ⁠Benin: Marcel Dandjinou (m.76, Saturnin Allagbé); Liam Omore, Yohan Roche (m.91, Amiro Amadou), Mohamed Tijani, Tamimou Ouorou (m.76, Charlemagne Azongnitode); Yamirou Ouorou (m.63, Matteo Ahlinvi), Sessi D’Almeida, Imourane Hassane (m.91, Sahid Ngobi), Junior Olaitan (m.76, Jodel Dossou), Rodolfo Aloko (m.91, Attidjikou Samadou); Aiyegun Tosin (m.63, Junior Olugbade). Seleccionador: Gernot Rohr. Goles: 1-0 m.48: Nicolás Otamendi. 2-0, m.61: Nicolás Paz. 3-0, m.70: Lionel Messi, de penalti. Árbitro: El chileno Fernando Vejar amonestó a Nicolás Otamendi y Mohamed Tijani. Incidencias: Partido amistoso en fecha FIFA disputado en el Estadio Monumental Antonio Vespucio Liberti, de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires.

data.title: Extienden alerta verde por 48 horas en San Pedro Sula y otros departamentos
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras. La Secretaría de Gestión de Riesgos y Contingencias Nacionales (Copeco) extendió por 48 horas la alerta verde para el Distrito Central , San Pedro Sula y Alianza, Valle , debido a las condiciones atmosféricas inestables que continuarán generando lluvias y chubascos en distintas zonas del país. La medida entrará en vigencia a partir de las 6:00 de la tarde de este martes 6 de octubre. Según el pronóstico de CENAOS , el ingreso de viento y humedad procedente del océano Pacífico favorecerá las precipitaciones, principalmente durante las horas de la tarde y noche. Las autoridades advirtieron que las lluvias podrían provocar incrementos en los niveles de ríos y quebradas, inundaciones repentinas y crecidas de riachuelos, especialmente en los sectores donde se registren mayores acumulados de lluvia. Además, existe riesgo de deslizamientos y derrumbes debido a la humedad de los suelos. Uno de los puntos donde se recomienda especial precaución es la carretera CA-5 hacia la zona sur, donde podrían presentarse afectaciones a la circulación vehicular. Ante estas condiciones, Copeco recomendó a la población mantenerse atenta a los comunicados oficiales y evitar cruzar ríos, quebradas o zonas inundadas durante los períodos de lluvia, con el objetivo de prevenir accidentes.

data.title: Policía revela posible hipótesis sobre la masacre que dejó tres muertos en Santa Bárbara
data.description: Quimistán, Santa Bárbara. La masacre de tres hombres en la comunidad de San Miguelito, Quimistán, Santa Bárbara, podría estar relacionada con una disputa entre estructuras criminales que operan en la zona, según una de las líneas que manejan las autoridades. El director general de la Policía Nacional, comisionado Rigoberto Oseguera Mass , se refirió este martes al caso y señaló que las primeras hipótesis apuntan a la posible participación de grupos criminales en un hecho relacionado con ajustes de cuentas o enfrentamientos entre estructuras. Sin embargo, el jefe policial pidió cautela al momento de establecer el móvil del triple crimen y afirmó que las investigaciones deberán determinar qué ocurrió y quiénes participaron. “Nosotros tenemos que ser muy serios para definir móviles, definir circunstancias alrededor de un hecho delictivo”, manifestó Oseguera Mass al referirse al caso. El comisionado aseguró que la Policía trabaja en la identificación de los responsables y advirtió que las estructuras criminales que operan en el sector serán objeto de acciones investigativas. “Muy seguramente de estos grupos criminales que se mueven en el sector, vamos a hacer sendas peticiones de declaratoria de asociaciones terroristas para estos grupos que infringen violencia y sangre en este sector”, sostuvo. El hecho ocurrió en la comunidad de San Miguelito, municipio de Quimistán, donde tres hombres fueron encontrados sin vida durante la madrugada. Las víctimas fueron identificadas como Raúl Martínez, de 40 años; Darwin Martínez, de 20; y Manuel Méndez, de 25 años, de acuerdo con la información proporcionada inicialmente por la Alcaldía de Quimistán. El reporte fue recibido alrededor de las 4:30 de la mañana, cuando el presidente del patronato de la comunidad comunicó a representantes de la municipalidad lo ocurrido. Tras conocer el caso, equipos de la Policía Nacional y personal de la Fiscalía se desplazaron hacia la zona para realizar las diligencias investigativas y el levantamiento de los cuerpos. Oseguera Mass señaló que el sector donde ocurrió el triple homicidio forma parte de una zona en la que las autoridades tienen identificadas distintas estructuras criminales. “Esa zona, ese corredor, esa franja que va paralela a la frontera con Guatemala, tiene sendos registros de acuerdo a nuestros inventarios de estructuras criminales”, afirmó. El director de la Policía Nacional indicó que las autoridades buscarán fortalecer las acciones contra esos grupos y adelantó que podrían solicitar su declaratoria como asociaciones terroristas, de acuerdo con los resultados de las investigaciones. Hasta ahora, no se ha informado de personas detenidas por el triple crimen. Otro de los aspectos que permanece bajo investigación es la posible relación entre las víctimas . Dos de los fallecidos, Raúl Martínez y Darwin Martínez, compartían apellido, pero las autoridades municipales señalaron inicialmente que no contaban con información suficiente para confirmar si existía un vínculo familiar entre ellos. La Policía Nacional y el Ministerio Público continuarán recopilando evidencias para establecer las circunstancias del hecho, identificar a los responsables y determinar el móvil del ataque. Mientras avanzan las investigaciones, la Alcaldía de Quimistán manifestó su disposición de acompañar a las familias de las tres víctimas.

data.title: Lo señalan como uno de los más violentos: cae presunto tercero al mando de la banda de El Mudo
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Honduras. La Policía capturó a Azael González, de 36 años, señalado como presunto tercero al mando de la banda de El Mudo, una estructura criminal investigada por asaltos, robos y otros hechos violentos en San Pedro Sula. El comisionado César Ruiz, jefe regional de la Policía de Investigación en San Pedro Sula, informó que González fue localizado mediante un proceso de vigilancia y seguimiento. Al momento de su requerimiento, según el reporte policial, portaba un arma de fuego de uso comercial que no estaba registrada en el Registro Nacional Balístico. “Precisamente estamos investigando por el delito de robo, robo con intimidación, robo con fuerza, robo con violencia”, explicó Ruiz al referirse a las investigaciones que mantienen las autoridades contra la estructura criminal. De acuerdo con el jefe policial, al trasladar a González a las instalaciones de la Dirección Policial de Investigaciones (DPI), se constató que estaría posiblemente vinculado con la banda de El Mudo, dedicada presuntamente a diferentes modalidades de robo. Ruiz señaló que González tenía medidas impuestas por un juez de San Pedro Sula desde 2023, entre ellas la prohibición de portar armas y de permanecer en lugares consumiendo bebidas alcohólicas. Según la Policía, al momento de su captura se encontraba en un establecimiento donde consumía bebidas alcohólicas y portaba un arma. “En el informe se hace referencia a que está quebrantando estas medidas para que el juez sea informado y que se le aplique lo que corresponde con respecto al cumplimiento de la condena que ya tenía en libertad”, manifestó Ruiz. El comisionado explicó que la vinculación de González con la estructura criminal forma parte de una investigación en curso, en la que las autoridades cuentan con declaraciones testimoniales y peritajes de dispositivos electrónicos. Estos indicios, dijo, serán presentados ante la autoridad competente para su valoración. Según Ruiz, la banda de El Mudo estaría integrada por personas que identifican previamente a sus víctimas y aprovechan momentos de vulnerabilidad para cometer los asaltos. El funcionario agregó que González es señalado dentro del grupo como una persona con un alto nivel de violencia. “Dentro de este grupo, se le señala como una persona de un alto nivel de violencia y eso también se le está reportando ya al fiscal para que sea tomado en consideración”, afirmó Ruiz. Las investigaciones policiales establecen que la estructura opera principalmente en zonas residenciales de alta plusvalía de San Pedro Sula y también estaría involucrada en asaltos a personas que salen de agencias bancarias. Las autoridades han perfilado a 13 presuntos integrantes, incluidos dos supuestos cabecillas, identificados como Héctor Moreno y Josué Lenín Chicas, quienes enfrentan procesos por robo agravado. La Policía también investiga la posible participación de integrantes de la banda en varios hechos violentos, entre ellos el asesinato de Juan Carlos Rodríguez Maldonado, conocido como Piola, exjugador del Real España, quien fue atacado a balazos y despojado de sus pertenencias el 23 de septiembre de 2026 en su negocio, frente al mercado Guamilito. Ruiz indicó que también se investiga la posible relación con otros casos, entre ellos el del abogado Edwin Salguero. “Se está siguiendo el proceso para tratar de obtener la suficiente información y ver si es posible vincular a los que ya se tienen identificados como parte de esta banda”, expresó el comisionado. Las autoridades sostienen que 11 presuntos integrantes de la estructura permanecen libres y que continúan las investigaciones para ubicarlos.
