data.title: Schmitz Cargobull to build EUR 25 mln factory in western Romania
data.description: The company will build a hall of approximately 23,500 square metres for the production of chassis subassemblies for semi-trailers and the assembly of complete vehicles, ebihoreanul.ro reported. Schmitz Cargobull has committed to investing at least EUR 25 mln and creating at least 200 jobs. “This amount refers strictly to the construction of the hall and its equipment. The land will be paid for separately,” Oradea mayor Florin Birta said. The project will therefore become the largest industrial investment attracted by Oradea in 2026. “It will certainly be the largest investment in Industrial Park IV. There are other plots here, but much smaller ones,” Birta said. Construction of the factory could begin next summer, with production starting in 2028. “Actual production would start in 2028,” Birta said. According to the mayor, the construction schedule depends primarily on preparing the site, which is currently crossed by two high-voltage power lines. “The relocation of one of the lines, which is the most important and affects them the most, is already in the tender procedure initiated by ADLO. The contract should be concluded this month, and the works should begin somewhere at the end of the year. In the meantime, the investor will design the factory so that the actual construction can begin next year,” Birta said. The cost of relocating the main high-voltage line is estimated at about RON 10 mln and will be covered by the municipality. The second power line will be relocated as part of the smart specialisation park project, financed by European funds. Separately, Oradea City Hall will arrange access to the site and bring utilities to the boundary of the plot.

data.title: Romanian state secretary warns of higher electricity prices this winter and in 2027
data.description: Romania will be affected by rising electricity prices on European markets, where record levels could be reached if the situation in the Middle East persists and the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, Buşoi said, as reported by Financialintelligence.ro . He also said that although Romania’s energy system has proved more resilient than specialists had expected, the outlook for the coming days is “very worrying”. Buşoi noted that both reactors at the Cernavodă Nuclear Power Plant remain offline, with no clear prospect of restarting, prolonging a situation that he said could push up electricity prices in the coming months. “If the situation prolongs in the Middle East and the strait remains closed, we expect record electricity prices in the European Union. As for Romania, everything depends on how long the situation with the closure of Cernavodă will last. We are also in contact with the main electricity suppliers,” Buşoi said.

data.title: Romania’s currency slips amid politics, fundamentals as country faces FX bond test
data.description: Sources cited by Economica.net estimated that Romania should have a designated government by October 16-17 in order to be able to issue FX bonds by November 7. Given the high level of US bond yields, Romania is expected to seek financing on other markets, including Europe and possibly Asia, such as Japan, the same sources said. The Romanian leu has continued to depreciate, with the euro crossing the RON 5.35 level from below RON 5.25 during the summer, following a sharp depreciation episode after the third attempt to form a government failed in Parliament on September 30. In its Macroeconomic Outlook for 2027, CFA Romania's analysts and survey respondents expect the leu to reach RON 5.4-5.5 per euro, with slightly higher depreciation risks towards the end of 2027. “This is an orderly depreciation, in the context of risks related to fiscal credibility and external shocks,” the CFA report said. Since last year, the leu has been on a nominal depreciation trend, which CFA specialists expect to continue. Thus, the leu is expected to depreciate by 2%-3% per year in the coming years. In real terms, however, the leu remains appreciated. Some market participants argue that an exchange rate of RON 5.5 per euro is therefore not that far away. In a recent report for investors, ING Bank said that “the central bank seems increasingly willing to allow greater flexibility in the EUR/RON exchange rate, which adds additional upside risk to this currency pair”. This is precisely what has happened since then, with the leu weakening further against the euro.

data.title: Romania’s retail sales up 0.9% y/y in August, driven by stronger fuel sales
data.description: Unexpectedly, given the much higher prices, the increase was driven by stronger fuel sales (+2.5% y/y), while the dynamics of food and non-food sales suggest continued pressure on household budgets: food sales contracted by 2.3% y/y, contrasting with a 2.7% increase in non-food sales. “Consumption is starting to show a clearer improvement in the third quarter, supporting our view that consumer spending should strengthen somewhat in the second half of the year,” according to a research note published by Erste Group. The 2.3% m/m increase in August, following a 0.7% m/m rise in July, could be interpreted as consumption gaining momentum. In perspective, however, this represents a short-term recovery that needs further confirmation before it can be seen as a sustainable trend. The two-month increase was again concentrated in fuel and non-food sales, which rose by 3.6% and 3.9%, respectively, compared with a 1.3% increase in food sales. The VAT rate hike in August 2025 had a significant impact on retail sales Retail sales were 4.7% lower in the 12 months to August 2026 than in the 12-month period to July 2025, before the VAT rate hike. The decline was broadly similar for food and non-food sales, at 5.0% and 5.1%, respectively, while the decline in fuel sales was comparatively smaller, at 3.0%. The correction in private consumption is consistent with the decline in real wages: real wages were 5.2% lower in the 12 months to July 2026, the latest period available, than in the 12 months preceding the VAT rate hike. High-frequency data show divergent consumption patterns High-frequency data are relevant for assessing consumer behaviour during the 13 months since the VAT rate hike. Non-food sales, which are more discretionary, fell sharply at key moments – in August following the VAT increase and again in January after the Christmas shopping period, when households became aware that annual wage adjustments were lower this year, where they were granted at all. They have subsequently recovered gradually during 2026, reflecting an improvement in consumer confidence, particularly among higher-income households. Food sales, which better reflect the budgets of households under greater financial pressure, have instead followed a gradual downward trend throughout the 13-month period. The pick-up in July-August came from a low base and therefore points to stabilisation at best. Fuel sales have also followed a broadly declining trend, although they increased in June, when higher wage income may have supported consumption, before recovering further in July-August. Consumption recovery expected in 2027 A recovery in private consumption is broadly expected in 2027. Public-sector wage and pension indexation in January, combined with lower inflation, should support real incomes and therefore stronger consumption next year. However, higher utility bills during the winter, elevated energy prices more generally and uncertainty over economic growth – with potential implications for private-sector wages – make the magnitude of the consumption recovery difficult to assess. Base effects could nevertheless produce relatively strong growth in the first half of next year.

data.title: Romanian president discusses EU budget, enlargement with Antonio Costa
data.description: Romanian president Nicușor Dan held a telephone conversation with European Council president Antonio Costa on Tuesday, October 6, to discuss the agenda of the upcoming EU leaders’ summit. Their talks covered the bloc’s future budget, economic competitiveness, energy prices, enlargement, and security challenges. “Romania wants an ambitious budget, even if additional resources are needed at EU level to support competitiveness and defence,” president Dan said in a post on Facebook . He added that cohesion policies would remain a priority for Romania. Moreover, the two officials also discussed EU enlargement and the membership prospects of Moldova and Ukraine. “We actively support the accession of the Republic of Moldova and Ukraine,” Nicușor Dan said. “Moldovans, alongside Ukrainians, deserve to be part of the Union, and this would significantly improve the security of Romania, the region and the Black Sea.” Other topics included Russia’s war against Ukraine and tensions in the Gulf. “The Council’s agenda is very busy because we have many important issues to discuss, from increasing economic competitiveness and energy prices to the future EU budget,” the Romanian president said. Nicușor Dan expressed confidence that EU leaders could make progress on the issues during the October 15-16 meeting.

data.title: 20 years in Romania, a new project for the community: Auchan supports the construction of 10 homes together with Habitat for Humanity
data.description: In the year in which it celebrates 20 years on the Romanian market, Auchan Romania, in partnership with Habitat for Humanity, is launching "Casute pentru casute" ("Little Houses for Homes"), a solidarity project supporting the construction of 10 homes for families in vulnerable situations. Auchan has allocated €625,000 to the project, with the homes to be built during 2026 and 2027 in two communities in Bacau and Prahova counties. Customers are invited to join the initiative by purchasing collectible construction toy houses available in Auchan stores, with the proceeds from their sale helping support the construction of real homes for families in need. Customers will find eight collectible house models in all Auchan stores, including MyAuchan Petrom stores and on auchan.ro. The houses can be purchased individually and, together, symbolically form a street. Each kit is priced at RON 39.99, and is available on the project page . "As we celebrate 20 years of Auchan in Romania, our gratitude towards our customers and communities is also reflected in the concrete things we do for them. Through 'Casute pentru casute', a simple gesture made while shopping can take on much greater meaning. We have already taken the first step by supporting the construction of the 10 homes, and now we are inviting our customers to join us. Building a small house at home together with loved ones can open up a conversation about what it means to have a safe place to live and about how we can support others. This idea also extends into schools, where children will build together and discover the meaning of solidarity. Quite simply, we thank everyone who chooses to be part of this project." said Raluca Mindirigiu, Marketing and Customer Relations Director, Auchan Romania. 1,000 educational sets to reach schools in 18 cities The project also includes an educational component. The retailer will distribute 1,000 educational building sets free of charge to schools in the 18 cities where the company operates hypermarkets. These sets are different from the collectible houses available for sale. The school sets contain a large number of pieces and do not follow a predefined model, allowing students to work together, as a class or in groups, to create their own interpretation of a house. The initiative is designed to encourage, in a creative way, conversations around empathy, solidarity and the importance of having a safe place to call home. "Our partnership with Habitat for Humanity began in 2023 and has grown year by year around one key objective: supporting families for whom access to a safe and decent home remains a major challenge. This year, by supporting the construction of 10 homes, we want to provide stability and a genuine new starting point for families in vulnerable situations. For us, the impact of this project can be seen in the beneficiaries' everyday lives, in the sense of security a home can provide and in the opportunity to live together with their families in better conditions. At the same time, Auchan colleagues will once again be able to join Habitat teams on construction sites and contribute directly to building these homes as volunteers." said Corina Dospinoiu-Imre, Sustainability Director, Auchan Romania. The project addresses both low-income families and people in situations of extreme vulnerability. The homes will be delivered fully built and finished, connected to utilities, and will include interior and exterior finishes, electrical, plumbing and heating systems, as well as essential sanitary fixtures. The houses are built using timber-frame structures, in duplex and quadruplex configurations. In an analysis conducted by Habitat for Humanity together with Carbon Tool for a duplex structure, the use of timber indicated a 17% reduction in embodied carbon emissions compared with a conventional concrete structure, demonstrating that affordable housing can also integrate solutions with a lower environmental impact. Construction site activities involve both volunteers and professional teams, with an estimated mix of approximately 70% volunteer contribution and 30% professional builders, all work being carried out under the coordination and supervision of specialists. Auchan Romania and Habitat for Humanity have been working together since 2023. The first project supported was the construction of the BufKids canteen in Buftea, designed for 50 children, through financial support of €40,000. In 2024, the partnership continued through the New Homes Moinesti and Hope Build Tutora projects, for which Auchan provided €115,000 in financial support. That same year, 120 Auchan Romania employees dedicated approximately 1,000 volunteer hours on Habitat construction sites in Iasi, contributing to the construction of homes for two families. In 2025, Auchan supported the Hope Build Berceni project with a financial contribution of €40,000. Through the "Casute pentru casute" project, the partnership enters a new stage in 2026, with the construction of the 10 homes in Moinesti and Berceni. Project video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pp6YBAgUb4k

"Our partnership with Habitat for Humanity began in 2023 and has grown year by year around one key objective: supporting families for whom access to a safe and decent home remains a major challenge. This year, by supporting the construction of 10 homes, we want to provide stability and a genuine new starting point for families in vulnerable situations. For us, the impact of this project can be seen in the beneficiaries' everyday lives, in the sense of security a home can provide and in the opportunity to live together with their families in better conditions. At the same time, Auchan colleagues will once again be able to join Habitat teams on construction sites and contribute directly to building these homes as volunteers." said Corina Dospinoiu-Imre, Sustainability Director, Auchan Romania. The project addresses both low-income families and people in situations of extreme vulnerability. The homes will be delivered fully built and finished, connected to utilities, and will include interior and exterior finishes, electrical, plumbing and heating systems, as well as essential sanitary fixtures. The houses are built using timber-frame structures, in duplex and quadruplex configurations. In an analysis conducted by Habitat for Humanity together with Carbon Tool for a duplex structure, the use of timber indicated a 17% reduction in embodied carbon emissions compared with a conventional concrete structure, demonstrating that affordable housing can also integrate solutions with a lower environmental impact. Construction site activities involve both volunteers and professional teams, with an estimated mix of approximately 70% volunteer contribution and 30% professional builders, all work being carried out under the coordination and supervision of specialists. Auchan Romania and Habitat for Humanity have been working together since 2023. The first project supported was the construction of the BufKids canteen in Buftea, designed for 50 children, through financial support of €40,000. In 2024, the partnership continued through the New Homes Moinesti and Hope Build Tutora projects, for which Auchan provided €115,000 in financial support. That same year, 120 Auchan Romania employees dedicated approximately 1,000 volunteer hours on Habitat construction sites in Iasi, contributing to the construction of homes for two families. In 2025, Auchan supported the Hope Build Berceni project with a financial contribution of €40,000. Through the "Casute pentru casute" project, the partnership enters a new stage in 2026, with the construction of the 10 homes in Moinesti and Berceni. data.title: Roughly 95% of Romanians would use RO Wallet, Interior Ministry survey says
data.description: A survey conducted by the Romanian Ministry of Internal Affairs showed that 95% of the Romanians surveyed would use RO Wallet , Romania’s digital identity wallet, according to an official press release released on Tuesday, October 6. The survey was conducted between September 13 and 27, 2026, and collected 3,065 complete responses. “The results show a very high level of interest: 85% of respondents say they will definitely use the application, while another 10% say they will probably use it. Only 3% still prefer paper documents,” the Ministry of Internal Affairs said. The identity card (96%), driving licence (94%) and health card (92%) are the documents that citizens most want in RO Wallet. Respondents would use the application mainly during traffic checks (89%), at public institution counters (84%), at the doctor’s or pharmacy (79%) and at the bank (78%). Abroad, 92% would use RO Wallet when travelling and at the border. Around 84% of respondents said they would want to see a history of who checked their data and when; 80% requested unlocking with a fingerprint or PIN, while 77% want to choose exactly what data they show and to whom, the release also said. “The survey results confirm that citizens want a secure platform for managing their documents. They want to be able to use the application both in Romania and in the European Union. We are building RO Wallet based on an essential principle: each citizen decides what data they transmit, to whom they transmit it and for what purpose. At the same time, use of the application remains private — no one can see whether a person uses RO Wallet, where they use it or for what purpose,” said police chief commissioner Răzvan-Iulian Jiga, director of DGCTI-MAI. RO Wallet is currently being rolled out, with the sandbox mode and the mobile test application set to be available starting October 31, 2026, for partners who will integrate it. In January, authorities will open remote enrollment for holders of the electronic identity card (CEI) by reading the chip using NFC and the card PIN. “The team is working on issuing and verifying identification data (PID), the application interface, the central system and the applications for Android and iOS. The technical documentation is published and continuously updated on GitHub,” the RO Wallet release said. RO Wallet will also be presented at EUDI Wallet Launchpad 2026, the European Commission event dedicated to national wallets, which takes place in Brussels on October 29-30.

data.title: Romanian prosecutors charge Iași mayor over alleged fictitious fuel oil purchase
data.description: Iași mayor Mihai Chirica has been formally charged with abuse of office in a case concerning missing fuel oil from the city’s heating company storage facilities, the National Anticorruption Directorate (DNA) announced . Nine other officials from Iași City Hall are also under investigation for alleged complicity in abuse of office and repeated intellectual forgery. According to prosecutors, Chirica approved a payment of RON 2.04 million (approximately EUR 380,000) from the local budget on May 27, 2022, while acting as mayor and the municipality’s chief authorising officer. The money was transferred to the National Administration of State Reserves and Special Issues for what the DNA described as “an allegedly fictitious purchase” of 542 tonnes of fuel oil. The quantity had previously been identified as missing, without legal approval, from state reserves stored at Termo Service, a company controlled by the Iași Local Council. The prosecutors allege that City Hall employees facilitated the payment by preparing documents claiming the fuel oil existed and had been received, although it had not actually been delivered. Officials are also suspected of drawing up and signing reception reports and discrepancy records that falsely certified the delivery of fuel oil. “The conduct described allegedly caused damage of RON 2,036,882 to the local budget of Iași municipality,” the DNA said. According to prosecutors, the payment also generated an undue benefit for the state reserves administration, which received the money and was able to remove the missing fuel from its accounting records. Termo Service allegedly benefited by having the shortage in its inventory covered on paper. The DNA imposed precautionary seizures on properties belonging to Mihai Chirica and other defendants as part of efforts to recover the alleged damage. The prosecutors stressed that formally charging the suspects is a procedural stage allowing evidence to be gathered and “cannot, under any circumstances, override the presumption of innocence.”

data.title: Romania’s EV charging network expands rapidly, but utilization remains low
data.description: Romania surpassed 10,000 public charging points for electric vehicles in August 2026, while the number of ultra-fast charging stations, with a capacity of at least 150 kW, has increased more than 45-fold over the past four years, reaching more than 2,060. However, the average utilization rate of charging stations is only 4-5%, according to the EV Charging Index 2026 – Currents of Change study conducted by Roland Berger in 34 countries. Romania’s charging infrastructure has grown more than sixfold over the past five years, and over the past three years it has expanded 1.4 times faster than the electric vehicle fleet. The fastest development has occurred in the ultra-fast charging station segment, with capacities of at least 150 kW. Their number increased from just 45 in 2022 to just over 2,060 in August 2026. During the same period, Romania reached 2,585 fast charging points, with capacities between 50 kW and 150 kW, and 5,420 points with capacities below 50 kW. The expansion of the network has been supported by both investments from private operators and European funding through the PNRR, the Modernization Fund and the Connecting Europe Facility. Currently, Romania has approximately 13 electrified vehicles for every public charging point, compared with a European average of 14 vehicles per point. At the same time, however, the average utilization rate of public charging stations is only around 4-5%. Roland Berger considers that this level of utilization indicates the existence of available capacity that can support the future growth in the number of electric vehicles without proportional additional investment in the short term. “Although electric vehicle adoption remains below the level of Western European countries, infrastructure progress and the entry of new manufacturers into the market create favorable conditions for the sector’s continued development in the coming years,” said Szabolcs Nemes, Managing Partner at Roland Berger Romania. Alongside the expansion of infrastructure, the market for 100% electric passenger cars returned to growth in 2026. In the first eight months of the year, 7,067 new BEV passenger cars were registered, 51% more than the 4,678 units in the same period last year. Their share of total new passenger car registrations increased from 4.9% to 8.2%. However, the market is still below the record level of 2023, when 15,318 new electric passenger cars were registered, with an adoption rate of 10.4%. An important part of the market comes from the used electric vehicle segment. Registrations of used BEVs increased from 398 units in 2021 to 4,342 in 2025, and in the first eight months of 2026 they exceeded 4,100 units, 55% above the level recorded in the same period of the previous year. According to the study, currently approximately one in two 100% electric passenger cars registered for the first time in Romania is used. Chinese manufacturers have also gained ground on the local market. The number of Chinese electric vehicle brands available in Romania has increased more than fivefold in recent years, and they now account for around 22% of new sales of 100% electric cars. Despite the growth in 2026, Romania remains behind mature European markets in terms of electric car adoption. In 2025, BEVs accounted for around 6% of new passenger car registrations in Romania, compared with 17% at the European level. In Norway, the share was 89%, in Denmark 64%, and in the Netherlands 42%. In terms of the vehicle fleet, 100% electric vehicles accounted for approximately 0.7% in Romania in 2025, compared with the European average of 3.4%. For the first half of 2026, Roland Berger estimates the national vehicle fleet at around 8.8 million passenger cars, of which 94% have conventional engines, 5.2% are hybrids and 0.8% are fully electric. According to a separate study by Global Payments Analysis examining the development of electric mobility and charging networks across Europe, Romania is a fast-growing market, with the number of public charging points increasing by approximately 33% year on year and a high share of DC charging infrastructure.

data.title: Lithuania Moves Closer Toward Scrapping Nuclear Weapons Ban
data.description: Lithuania moved closer toward lifting its long-standing nuclear weapons ban, after the amendment passed its first reading on Tuesday, Oct. 6, with 106-18 votes in favor. The country’s Constitution currently prohibits weapons of mass destruction and foreign military bases to be stationed on its territory. data.title: Blood, Bombs & Billions
data.description: TEHRAN- The US-Israeli war against Iran was not merely a military and geopolitical crisis; it also created a major economic shock. According to an estimate by the US Congressional Budget Office (CBO), the direct cost of US combat operations against Iran had reached approximately $38 billion by August 1, 2026. That figure includes the cost of replacing expended munitions and lost equipment, increased flight hours, military operations, and higher fuel costs. It does not include costs borne by other federal agencies or the war’s longer-term economic consequences.

data.title: DSP o Maquiavélico Ganancioso
data.description: Guineenses, mais uma vez, venho para vos alertar sobre o perigo que Domingos Simões Pereira representa para a Guiné-Bissau. Faço esse alerta a todos os guineenses sem exceção que se encontre no país ou no estrangeiro, ao PAIGC em especial e na pessoa do Cipriano Cassamá em concreto. Alerta esse sobre o verdadeiro DSP, o verdadeiro espírito que move esse sujeito, o qual alguns ainda continuam a acreditar para não dizer adorar. Domingos Simões Pereira é um manipulador, um verdadeiro chantagista e calculista provavelmente, tipo de comportamento que ultrapassa o nível de psicopata. U m ambicioso desmedido, um verdadeiro criminoso que sabe como e quando cometer o crime. Ele jamais coabitaria não só com JOMAV, assim como com qualquer presidente que seria eleito, a não ser o que ele apoiou disfarçadamente. Isto porque ele tem sua própria agenda, e o PAIGC é simplesmente uma plataforma para sua concretização. DSP jamais coabitaria com JOMAV porque o seu candidato preferido era o Paulo Gomes e sempre será, o qual juntamente com Tchitchi vão delineando mecanismo de modo a serem os novos donos da Guiné-Bissau. Segundo eles este é um processo a médio prazo, e é preciso coragem e paciência para concretiza-lo. Ganhar o congresso não importa em que circunstância e ter novamente o partido na mão, é uma fase concluída em proveito deles, enquanto verdadeiros militantes do PAIGC estão a bater palmas. Depois dessa eleição legislativa, não importa o resultado, o Cipriano Cassama que se prepare a mala ou fica de bico fechado, pois o candidato preferido para o partido será o Paulo Gomes, e esse sim deve ter a voz dentro do partido. DSP é um ambicioso desmedido, nunca teve consideração por ninguém, JOMAV muito menos, o sujeito é um maquiavélico nato, Cipriano Casama será descartado quando menos esperar podes tomar a nota. Guineenses, falar do Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi é falar do MCCI e demais outras organizações e personalidades camufladas no nosso país. Esses dois indivíduos são os principais financiadores do MCCI e demais outras personalidades boca de aluguel na cidade de Bissau. O MCCI, Milícia idealizado por JBV e DSP, agora financiado e dirigido por "futuro triângulo do poder" ou seja, "DSP, Paulo Gomes e Tchitchi", têm 3 principais objectivos: 1º Perturbar a ordem pública em nome da cidadania, difamar e tentar descredibilizar qualquer que seja organizações ou indivíduos não alinhados ao triângulo, de modo a suportar suas caminhadas na busca do poder. 2º Caso se concretize o objectivo do triângulo, o papel da Milícia do MCCI passará a ser de vigilância constante a todos os adversários de modo a garantir falsa paz social e o poder de controlo. 3º Tentar ganhar credibilidade junto das organizações internacionais e regionais, através de suas visitas e actividades de fachada, para quando houver as tais actividades de perturbações de ordem pública, poderem ganhar notoriedade. Mas isso não deve preocupar ninguém, pois estão bem identificados e bem caçados, dentro e fora da Guiné-Bissau. Não tenho nada contra ninguém, mas quem continuar a perturbar verdadeira paz social dos guineenses em troca de benefícios como sempre foi nos últimos anos dessa crise, e que sempre tenho tolerado, então que fique claro "estou firme e determinado para tudo e todos". Para finalizar, gostaria de vos deixar uma reflexão com a seguinte frase: " Domingos Simões Pereira é um perigo grave para o futuro do país ". Isto porque publicar aqui tudo que é necessário para provar ou sustentar a razão dessa frase, só pode agravar ainda mais a paz social que tanto necessitamos. Chega, chega não podemos continuar a viver nessa turbulência vida toda, meus irmãos guineenses, não é saudável, é tóxico, não é justo para um povo que tanto sofreu. data.title: DSP, UM PERIGO GRAVE PARA FUTURO DO PAÍS
data.description: Os meios de comunicação também são as formas de manipulação mais utilizadas pelos poderes políticos, dado o seu impacto social. As informações são manipuladas não apenas tendo em vista omitir factos relevantes, mas também distorcer o conteúdo da informação veiculada, produzir ou forjar a opinião pública, de modo que a mesma se ajuste às ideias dos gananciosos. A única forma dos cidadãos evitarem cair nestes processos de manipulação é tornarem-se mais vigilantes em relação às instituições democráticas e aos órgãos de informação, adoptando uma atitude de permanente reflexão crítica sobre a informação que lhes é fornecida. Na Guiné-Bissau, nos últimos anos, cresceu exponencialmente o número de pessoas mediocres, pessoas sem escrúpulos ligadas à produção de rádios e outros meios de comunicação com influencia na nossa sociedade, gente que apesar da sua enorme influência na sociedade, trabalha na mais completa impunidade e sem qualquer controlo ético/democrático. Obcecado pelo poder, ciente da dificuldade do povo guineense em avaliar informações, ciente do poder dos instrumentos de comunicação, Domingos Simões Pereira (DSP) nunca menosprezou esses instrumentos para atingir seu objectivo, sempre usou-os de forma desonesta como agora está a fazer tudo por tudo para manter no controlo desses veicúlos, mesmo que isso custe a vida dos outros. Governou na corrupção, no nepotismo e no desvios de somas astronómicas do dinheiro de povo, que muito serviria para investimentos na saúde, educação e outros serviços publicos, para beneficiar familiares e amigos. Finge que preocupa com os problemas do país, mas só engana o povo honesto, humilde e trabalhador que infelizmente sofre muito, não sei até quando, devido a sua paciência e tolerância aos governantes como DSP, criminoso travestido em politico que vive na custa de povo e acima de tudo ainda fa-lo refem do próprio suor. Roubou e decepcionou tanto não só aos guineenses assim como a comunidade internacional que sempre acreditou que o sujeito era ideal para ajudar esse povo a sair do ciclo de sofrimento que parece infinito. Foi demitido, não conformou e está a fazer tudo na medida do possível para continuar a complicar a vida dos guineenses. Razão disso é que depois de perder a batalha nos meios de comunicações mais modernos nomeadamente os blogues onde investiu grandes somas do dinheiro de povo, para fazer a lavagem cerebral dos menos instruídos e não só. Fugiu do facebook onde sempre frequentava e comunicava com todos tentado passar a mensagem de um politico moderno e aberto a diálogo/opiniões, mas que afinal era simplesmente um falso modernista. Caiu a mascara e já não consegue enganar ninguem, pois a sua credibilidade está abaixo de zero, para não dizer outra coisa. Camaradas, para conhecimento geral, com o dinheiro roubado que custou suor de povo guineense, DSP decidiu avançar com um outro novo plano maquiavelico, para criar a sua própria estação de rádio. Documento António Aly Silva » aaly.silva@gmail.com » aaly_silva@hotmail.com » Tel. (+245) 668 31 13

data.title: DSP não respeita os antigos combatentes e sempre usou e abusou desses camaradas. Prova disso é que continuou a governar mesmo já com Carlos Correia como primeiro ministro. Usou até o cadáver de Carmem Perreira para promover sua imagem, pois é sabido que a malograda como sendo antigo combatente e membro do PAIGC o corpo só deveria passar por ANP e sede do partido e nunca na Primatura como aconteceu, e por cima de tudo com indivíduos alí barricados por vontade própria vandalizando instituição do estado o que demonstra uma clara promoção ao anarquismo. Não respeitou nem o Pai da Nação(ALC), nem o PR quanto mais o formalismo de um estado de direito democrático, prova disso mais uma vez, o ganancioso após o PR ter depositado coroas de flores no túmulo de ALC no dia dos heróis nacionais, reuniu os seus "gangs" para o mesmo efeito, conseguiu até mobilizar um dos familiares do Pai da Nação para lhe acompanhar tudo isso para manipular e dividir os guineenses "guineenses ku udjus fitchadu" para os seus intereses obscuros.

data.title: Budget : le Togo battu par des pays plus pauvres que lui
data.description: Le dernier rapport de la Banque mondiale sur l’économie africaine place le Togo au 22e rang sur 46 pour son déficit budgétaire et au 29e pour sa dette. Le pays est loin de l’image de bon élève souvent mise en avant, et des économies plus pauvres et plus fragiles le devancent. La Banque mondiale a publié en octobre 2026 son rapport « État des lieux de l’économie africaine », consacré cette année à l’intelligence artificielle. En page 96, le tableau A.2 des annexes macroéconomiques remet le Togo à sa place. Son déficit budgétaire est estimé à 3,4 % du PIB […]
